checks.text: With no inputs, the page shows the heading "BMI Calculator", the text "Enter your height and weight to calculate BMI", and the result area displays "BMI: —".

Typing 170 in the field labelled "Height" and 65 in the field labelled "Weight" with the unit select set to "Metric (cm, kg)" shows "BMI: 22.5" in the result summary and "Normal weight" in the category label.

Typing 5 in the field labelled "Height" and 10 in the field labelled "Weight" with the unit select set to "Imperial (ft, lbs)" shows "BMI: 21.8" in the result summary and "Normal weight" in the category label.

Typing 150 in the field labelled "Height" and 80 in the field labelled "Weight" with the unit select set to "Metric (cm, kg)" shows "BMI: 35.6" in the result summary and "Obese" in the category label.

Typing 180 in the field labelled "Height" and 50 in the field labelled "Weight" with the unit select set to "Metric (cm, kg)" shows "BMI: 15.4" in the result summary and "Underweight" in the category label.
Typing 0 in the field labelled "Weight" and clicking the button "Calculate" shows the message "Weight must be greater than 0" and the result area still displays "BMI: —".
The breakdown table shows rows for "Underweight", "Normal weight", "Overweight", and "Obese" with their BMI ranges; when BMI is 22.5 the row "Normal weight" is highlighted and the others are not.

Typing 175 in the field labelled "Height" and 70 in the field labelled "Weight" with the unit select set to "Metric (cm, kg)" shows "BMI: 22.9" in the result summary and the chart bar for "Normal weight" is filled to 100% while other bars are at 0%.
Reload keeps the last calculation: after entering Height 170, Weight 65 in Metric units and seeing "BMI: 22.5", reloading the page still shows "BMI: 22.5" and "Normal weight" in the result summary.
